title: First paid gig and supportive parents
summary: Playing pops concerts with symphonies, then his first pay of about $70 with high school band director; parents chaperoned underage gigs. Born 1970.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Can you remember the first time you made money playing a gig, and how much was it?

I think the first time I actually made money, I think it probably had to be about ninth grade I think. I had already been doing some classical performances, like orchestras and stuff, and my junior high school orchestra teacher had even gotten some of her students who excelled to perform, to do some performances, like pops concerts with the professional symphonies. We’d play with the Marshall Texas Symphony and the Shreveport Symphony early on. But I wasn’t making any money but I was there playing with the other professionals, which was really awesome. It was very meaningful for a kid. But I think when I met my high school band director, Larry Pinell was made I was kind of like going out playing gigs, like when I did something with his band. I don’t know, and I made probably like 70 bucks or something. That was a lot of money. That got me hooked pretty quickly.
That’s 66 more dollars than I made on my first gig.

It was a lot of money. And my parents, they were always very supportive and took me to lessons and everything. So then of course I started playing the gigs, you know, any of the ones that — my parents would go, so that was obviously very good — and be there to make sure — I was underage you know. So there were a few clubs that I performed in

and I shouldn’t have been there, at least legally I shouldn’t have been there, in terms of the age requirement to get in there. But we did all kinds of things. We performed things like debutante balls and weddings and even some club things.
